solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird of beautiful markings

indicators.note: the bird is made of letters drawn from the run of the following two words

explanation.surface: A bird admired for its lovely plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull-like seabird of the petrel family nesting on northern cliffs.

clue.text: Panic over colours in cake

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over the next, so it comes first

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
a jack is a flag, as are colours

explanation.surface: Someone panics about the icing colours on a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A British oat bar baked with butter and syrup; in the US the word names a pancake.

clue.text: Much less shelter protecting hooker

indicators.note: the shelter word wraps around the hooker as if shielding it

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind
a talon is a claw that hooks prey

explanation.surface: A refuge offers much less protection to a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooker' tempts a rugby or street reading; it is a claw.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom used after a negative: 'I can't walk, never mind run' means much less run.

clue.text: Declare spelunker's missing the surface

indicators.note: the top letter of the cave explorer word is lost, as if never reaching the surface

parts.note: a spelunker is a caver, someone who explores caves; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A cave explorer is said to be lost underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to state firmly or assert something as true.

clue.text: A nasty person has reversed schedule, stirrer

parts.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person

indicators.note: the schedule word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person has switched round the timetable, making trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker who stirs up unrest is an agitator.

clue.text: Heroine at sea offering prayer to sweetheart

parts.note: grace is a short prayer said before a meal
darling is a term for a loved one

explanation.surface: A woman sailing says a prayer for her beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling was a lighthouse keeper's daughter who helped rescue shipwreck survivors off Northumberland in 1838.
explanation.definitionFit: She is famous as a British heroine of a sea rescue.

clue.text: Embarrassing lunge stops short with erotic dancing

indicators.note: the letters dance into a new order
the lunge word halts before its final letter

explanation.surface: An awkward lurch cut off amid some racy moves on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops short' cuts LUNGE to LUNG; with EROTIC, 'dancing' rearranges the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: So cringe-making that it makes one's toes curl, hence acutely awkward.

clue.text: Roller pressing on in Irish county

indicators.note: the roller word bears down around the second word, holding it within

parts.note: a tyre is something that rolls along

explanation.surface: A steamroller pressing on through rural Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county of Northern Ireland, one of the six in Ulster.

clue.text: Leave one's post and go upstairs?

definitions.meaning: to give up work or a job for good
to head off to bed for the night

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both stopping work for good and going to bed.

clue.text: One's rousing article — so not us?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
them is the other lot, not us

explanation.surface: A stirring essay asks whether it is about outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's rousing' reads as a song that stirs; 'so' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A national or sporting song meant to stir a crowd.

clue.text: Rodent discovering earth in temple

indicators.note: the earth word goes inside the temple word

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
terra is Latin for earth

explanation.surface: A rat is found burrowing in the soil of a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The name for a water vole, a river-bank rodent.

clue.text: Take responsibility, as should a 13 across?

definitions.meaning: to confront the consequences of one's actions
a person turning a musician's pages must look at the sheet music

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting blame; literally a page-turner at a recital faces the score.

clue.text: A bit to carry left in jar

indicators.note: the small-amount word holds the letter for left inside

parts.note: a jot is a very small amount

explanation.surface: Some cargo is put into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a pot, but it is the verb meaning shake.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to shake suddenly, a jolt.

clue.text: Contact artist in absorbing book

parts.note: to page someone is to contact them by pager or call
J. M. W. Turner was the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: Reaching a painter while engrossed in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping novel that keeps readers flipping on to the next leaf.

clue.text: Two little peas, say, very soft?

definitions.meaning: two small letters p, pp, is the score marking for this
the musical term for playing very quietly

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction meaning very quiet, abbreviated pp in a score.

clue.text: Handsome — so worth examining?

definitions.meaning: as in a handsome sum, meaning large
read as able to be considered, i.e. worth thinking about

explanation.definitionFit: A handsome profit is a sizeable one; jokily, the word also reads as fit to be considered.

clue.text: Instrument integral to work

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instrument essential to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument: a steel bar bent into a three-sided shape and struck.

clue.text: Giant sort of painting turning up, as carved design

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a fresh order
in a down entry the painting word is read upwards

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: A huge sort of canvas turning up as a sculpted pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GIANT into INTAG; 'turning up' reverses OIL to LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A design cut into the surface of a gem or stone, the opposite of a cameo.

clue.text: Where marathon competitors are seen, finally

definitions.meaning: runners in a marathon are literally in a long race
an idiom meaning eventually, over time

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in the end, with a literal reading of being part of a lengthy race.

clue.text: Idiot raising Manx cat before dog, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down entry the shortened cat word is lifted, read upwards
a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: a puma is a big cat
a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A fool picks up a tailless cat ahead of the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' docks PUMA to PUM; 'raising' turns it to MUP.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a foolish person, from the puppet show.

clue.text: Compound sat in hole for laboratory device

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the hole word

parts.note: a gap is a hole or opening

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A chemical compound sitting in a hole in a lab.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve on a lab bench supplying fuel to a Bunsen burner.

clue.text: Modest problem contained by using an orderly

indicators.note: the problem word is held inside the reordered letters
put in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A humble hospital orderly sets a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital worker in the surface, but here it is an adjective meaning put into order, and 'contained by' wraps the result around the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: not pretentious or showy.

clue.text: Drop a story

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: Dropping a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tale, originally an Icelandic heroic narrative.

clue.text: High-pitched noise, buzzer with power

parts.note: a bee buzzes
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A buzzer emitting a shrill sound when switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: A short high electronic tone, as from a horn or alarm.

clue.text: Most nutty pastries with extravagant filling, beginning to tempt

indicators.note: the extravagant word goes inside the pastries word

parts.note: pies are pastries
OTT is short for over the top

indicators.note: only the first letter of the tempt word is taken

explanation.surface: Wildly rich pastries with a lavish filling, to tempt the crazed.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: potty means crazy, so the superlative means craziest.

clue.text: Boy and girl cat

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A boy, a girl and their cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic cat breed with a spotted coat, or the Bengal tiger.

clue.text: Outstanding spinner has not caught Hampshire's opener

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the opening letter of the county name is taken

explanation.surface: A brilliant spin bowler hasn't caught the Hampshire opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county with a cricket team; 'spinner' and 'opener' sound like cricket, but one is a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym for first-rate or excellent.

clue.text: Issue about parking with old driver's assistant

indicators.note: the issue word goes round the parking letter

parts.note: seed means offspring, issue

explanation.surface: A problem with parking for an elderly motorist's aide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' suggests a problem; it is offspring. A speedo is a speedometer.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for speedometer, the dial that helps a driver keep to the limit.
